system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller position | What Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | General Warranty Claims capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | **25% / AUD 6m**. The 20% fallback requires Amelia Frost’s prior written authority identifying the draft; none is given. | **Reject; seek 25% / AUD 6m** — the stated fallback is not authorised. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis; AUD 250,000 basket, with only the excess recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis; AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery **from the first dollar once exceeded**. | **Reject; seek playbook thresholds and tipping-basket recovery** — Seller’s figures are materially higher and its basket is deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months; Seller also proposes all claim limits apply unless expressly stated otherwise. | 24 months after Completion; no general limit should silently override separate regimes. | **Reject; seek 24 months and explicit regime carve-outs** — 18 months is an unauthorised fallback and the proposed default risks overriding other claims. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; require separate fundamental/title terms** — Seller’s proposal collapses protections the playbook requires to remain distinct. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this position cannot be waived. | **Reject; require the full carve-out** — the Seller’s all-Claims language risks applying restrictions to conduct that must remain carved out. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific disclosures also given. | Specific fair disclosure; reject deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject general disclosure; retain only specific fair disclosures** — broad deemed disclosure would undermine warranty protection. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known to Buyer or advisers, including data-room or public-record matters. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusion. If a qualifier is accepted, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete the blanket exclusion** — it improperly shifts broad diligence and public-record risk to Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied is included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for this material customer. | **Reject; make both effective consent and condition satisfaction evidence Completion requirements** — delivery alone does not establish the conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it is unrepaid and no final discharge is included. | Current payout; direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases. Any post-Completion release requires an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost’s approval. | **Reject post-Completion release; require repayment and effective release at Completion** — the facility remains outstanding and no discharge is evidenced. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are not separately itemised in the funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or Seller-funded; funds flow must not silently omit them. | **Require itemisation or Seller funding** — the disclosed conditional bonuses are omitted from the draft funds flow and on-cost exposure is unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Existing indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-004 ties transfer to cleared payment of every SOW3 fee; DD-010’s AUD 180,000 is not independent bank verification, and no payment receipt or assignment is included. | Broaden the indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not treat AUD 180,000 as independently verified either way. | **Reject the narrow indemnity; broaden it and preserve the cure** — the record does not establish payment or assignment, nor independently verify the amount. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Seller calls DD-006 preliminary and not expected to be material; no confirmed breach or loss is established. | Preserve logs, investigate and provide updates; do not assume a confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. | **Require preservation, investigation and updates without prejudging liability** — the record is preliminary and leaves access, scope and notification unresolved. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 renewals described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess the three renewals together; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt** — timing and scope are disclosed, but the commercial and accounting treatment is not established. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Seller says Tax/IP are settled under the general regime and proposes broad limits on all Claims. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden general-regime override. | **Reject the blanket general-regime treatment** — broad language could collapse distinct claim categories and protections. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register recording Seller as holder of 100%. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof. | **Require independent verification** — the register identifies the source relied on but does not itself provide independent proof. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller considers Tax/IP positions settled under its proposed general regime. | Tax/IP terms remain open; do not assume unlimited liability or resolution. | **Keep open for negotiation; do not accept settlement or assume unlimited liability** — the Seller’s assertion is not Buyer authority or an agreed resolution. |

The Seller’s “STANDARD,” “reviewed and cleared,” and “accepted” labels are counterparty assertions, not Buyer approvals. The Buyer should assess the full package against the playbook rather than limit review to items labelled “OPEN.”
=== END ADVICE ===
